audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Ruth threshing-floor plan, nighttime encounter, wing/redeemer request, nearer redeemer, grain gift, and waiting narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Naomi's rest/security aim, threshing-floor setting, washing/anointing/clothing instructions, feet/place euphemism question, Ruth's nighttime vulnerability, direct self-identification, spread-your-wing request, hesed and age/power language, eshet-hayil recognition, nearer-redeemer procedure, oath, secrecy, six-barley measure, pronoun variant, and Naomi's final counsel.

verses.restored: Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, My daughter, should I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?

familiar.text: Then Naomi her mother in law said unto her, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee?

modern.text: One day Ruth’s mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, should I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?

original.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לָ֖הּ נָעֳמִ֣י חֲמוֹתָ֑הּ בִּתִּ֞י הֲלֹ֧א אֲבַקֶּשׁ לָ֛ךְ מָנ֖וֹחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽיטַב לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Now, is not Boaz our kinsman, with whose young women you were? Look, he is winnowing barley tonight at threshing floor.

familiar.text: And now is not Boaz of our kindred, with whose maidens thou wast? Behold, he winnoweth barley to night in the threshingfloor.

modern.text: Now is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been working, a relative of ours? In fact, tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֲלֹ֥א בֹ֨עַז֙ מֹֽדַעְתָּ֔נוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖ית אֶת נַעֲרוֹתָ֑יו הִנֵּה ה֗וּא זֹרֶ֛ה אֶת גֹּ֥רֶן הַשְּׂעֹרִ֖ים הַלָּֽיְלָה

verses.restored: Wash yourself, anoint yourself, put your garments upon you, and go down to threshing floor. Do not make yourself known to man until he has finished eating and drinking.

familiar.text: Wash thyself therefore, and anoint thee, and put thy raiment upon thee, and get thee down to the floor: but make not thyself known unto the man, until he shall have done eating and drinking.

modern.text: Therefore wash yourself, put on perfume, and wear your best clothes. Go down to the threshing floor, but do not let the man know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.

original.text: וְרָחַ֣צְתְּ וָסַ֗כְתְּ וְשַׂ֧מְתְּ שמלתך עָלַ֖יִךְ וירדתי הַגֹּ֑רֶן אַל תִּוָּדְעִ֣י לָאִ֔ישׁ עַ֥ד כַּלֹּת֖וֹ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וְלִשְׁתּֽוֹת

verses.restored: When he lies down, know place where he lies. Go, uncover place of his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what you shall do.

familiar.text: And it shall be, when he lieth down, that thou shalt mark the place where he shall lie, and thou shalt go in, and uncover his feet, and lay thee down; and he will tell thee what thou shalt do.

modern.text: When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go in and uncover his feet, and lie down, and he will explain to you what you should do.”

original.text: וִיהִ֣י בְשָׁכְב֗וֹ וְיָדַ֨עַתְּ֙ אֶת הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשְׁכַּב שָׁ֔ם וּבָ֛את וְגִלִּ֥ית מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו ושכבתי וְהוּא֙ יַגִּ֣יד לָ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעַשִֽׂין

verses.restored: She said to her, All that you say to me, I will do.

familiar.text: And she said unto her, All that thou sayest unto me I will do.

modern.text: “I will do everything you say,” Ruth answered.

original.text: וַתֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֶ֑יהָ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמְרִ֥י אֶֽעֱשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: She went down to threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her.

familiar.text: And she went down unto the floor, and did according to all that her mother in law bade her.

modern.text: So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had instructed her to do.

original.text: וַתֵּ֖רֶד הַגֹּ֑רֶן וַתַּ֕עַשׂ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוַּ֖תָּה חֲמוֹתָֽהּ

verses.restored: Boaz ate and drank, and his heart was good. He went to lie at end of grain heap. She came quietly, uncovered place of his feet, and lay down.

familiar.text: And when Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of corn: and she came softly, and uncovered his feet, and laid her down.

modern.text: After Boaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. Then Ruth went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אכַל בֹּ֤עַז וַיֵּשְׁתְּ֙ וַיִּיטַ֣ב לִבּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕א לִשְׁכַּ֖ב בִּקְצֵ֣ה הָעֲרֵמָ֑ה וַתָּבֹ֣א בַלָּ֔ט וַתְּגַ֥ל מַרְגְּלֹתָ֖יו וַתִּשְׁכָּֽב

verses.restored: At middle of night, the man trembled and turned himself, and look—a woman was lying at place of his feet.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at midnight, that the man was afraid, and turned himself: and, behold, a woman lay at his feet.

modern.text: At midnight, Boaz was startled, turned over, and there lying at his feet was a woman!

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַלַּ֔יְלָה וַיֶּחֱרַ֥ד הָאִ֖ישׁ וַיִּלָּפֵ֑ת וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִשָּׁ֔ה שֹׁכֶ֖בֶת מַרְגְּלֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: He said, Who are you? She said, I am Ruth, your servant. Spread your wing over your servant, because you are a redeemer.

familiar.text: And he said, Who art thou? And she answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.

modern.text: “Who are you?” he asked. “I am your servant Ruth,” she replied. “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer. ”

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִי אָ֑תּ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אָנֹכִי֙ ר֣וּת אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֤ כְנָפֶ֨ךָ֙ עַל אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ כִּ֥י גֹאֵ֖ל אָֽתָּה

verses.restored: He said, Blessed are you by YHWH, my daughter. You have made your latter covenant-kindness better than first by not going after young men, whether poor or rich.

familiar.text: And he said, Blessed be thou of the LORD, my daughter: for thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich.

modern.text: Then Boaz said, “May the LORD bless you, my daughter. You have shown more kindness now than before, because you have not run after the younger men, whether rich or poor.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרוּכָ֨ה אַ֤תְּ לַֽיהוָה֙ בִּתִּ֔י הֵיטַ֛בְתְּ חַסְדֵּ֥ךְ הָאַחֲר֖וֹן מִן הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן לְבִלְתִּי לֶ֗כֶת אַחֲרֵי֙ הַבַּ֣חוּרִ֔ים אִם דַּ֖ל וְאִם עָשִֽׁיר

verses.restored: Now, my daughter, do not fear. All that you say I will do for you, because all gate of my people knows that you are a woman of strength and worth.

familiar.text: And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.

modern.text: And now do not be afraid, my daughter. I will do for you whatever you request, since all my fellow townspeople know that you are a woman of noble character.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה בִּתִּי֙ אַל תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמְרִ֖י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה לָּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ כָּל שַׁ֣עַר עַמִּ֔י כִּ֛י אֵ֥שֶׁת חַ֖יִל אָֽתְּ

verses.restored: Now, indeed, it is true that I am a redeemer, but there is also a redeemer nearer than I.

familiar.text: And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I.

modern.text: Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ כִּ֣י אָמְנָ֔ם כִּ֥י אם גֹאֵ֖ל אָנֹ֑כִי וְגַ֛ם יֵ֥שׁ גֹּאֵ֖ל קָר֥וֹב מִמֶּֽנִּי

verses.restored: Stay this night. In morning, if he will redeem you, good—let him redeem. But if he does not desire to redeem you, then I will redeem you, as YHWH lives. Lie down until morning.

familiar.text: Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the LORD liveth: lie down until the morning.

modern.text: Stay here tonight, and in the morning, if he wants to redeem you, good. Let him redeem you. But if he does not want to redeem you, as surely as the LORD lives, I will. Now lie here until morning.”

original.text: לִ֣ינִי הַלַּ֗יְלָה וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ אִם יִגְאָלֵ֥ךְ טוֹב֙ יִגְאָ֔ל וְאִם לֹ֨א יַחְפֹּ֧ץ לְגָֽאֳלֵ֛ךְ וּגְאַלְתִּ֥יךְ אָנֹ֖כִי חַי יְהוָ֑ה שִׁכְבִ֖י עַד הַבֹּֽקֶר

verses.restored: She lay at place of his feet until morning and arose before one could recognize another. He said, Let it not be known that the woman came to threshing floor.

familiar.text: And she lay at his feet until the morning: and she rose up before one could know another. And he said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor.

modern.text: So she lay down at his feet until morning, but she got up before anyone else could recognize her. Then Boaz said, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.”

original.text: וַתִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מרגלתו עַד הַבֹּ֔קֶר וַתָּ֕קָם בטרום יַכִּ֥יר אִ֖ישׁ אֶת רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַל יִוָּדַ֔ע כִּי בָ֥אָה הָאִשָּׁ֖ה הַגֹּֽרֶן

verses.restored: He said, Bring cloak that is upon you and hold it. She held it, and he measured six measures of barley and placed it upon her. Then he went into city.

familiar.text: Also he said, Bring the vail that thou hast upon thee, and hold it. And when she held it, he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her: and she went into the city.

modern.text: And he told her, “Bring the shawl you are wearing and hold it out.” When she did so, he shoveled six measures of barley into her shawl. Then he went into the city.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָ֠בִי הַמִּטְפַּ֧חַת אֲשֶׁר עָלַ֛יִךְ וְאֶֽחֳזִי בָ֖הּ וַתֹּ֣אחֶז בָּ֑הּ וַיָּ֤מָד שֵׁשׁ שְׂעֹרִים֙ וַיָּ֣שֶׁת עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיָּבֹ֖א הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: She came to her mother-in-law, who said, How did it go with you, my daughter? She told her all that the man had done for her.

familiar.text: And when she came to her mother in law, she said, Who art thou, my daughter? And she told her all that the man had done to her.

modern.text: When Ruth returned to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked her, “How did it go, my daughter?” Then Ruth told her all that Boaz had done for her.

original.text: וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל חֲמוֹתָ֔הּ וַתֹּ֖אמֶר מִי אַ֣תְּ בִּתִּ֑י וַתַּ֨גֶּד לָ֔הּ אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָֽשָׂה לָ֖הּ הָאִֽישׁ

verses.restored: She said, These six measures of barley he gave to me, because he said to me, Do not go empty to your mother-in-law.

familiar.text: And she said, These six measures of barley gave he me; for he said to me, Go not empty unto thy mother in law.

modern.text: And she said, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”

original.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר שֵׁשׁ הַשְּׂעֹרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה נָ֣תַן לִ֑י כִּ֚י אָמַ֣ר אַל תָּב֥וֹאִי רֵיקָ֖ם אֶל חֲמוֹתֵֽךְ

verses.restored: Naomi said, Sit, my daughter, until you know how matter will fall, because man will not rest unless he completes matter today.

familiar.text: Then said she, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest, until he have finished the thing this day.

modern.text: “Wait, my daughter,” said Naomi, “until you find out how things go, for he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ שְׁבִ֣י בִתִּ֔י עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֵּֽדְעִ֔ין אֵ֖יךְ יִפֹּ֣ל דָּבָ֑ר כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשְׁקֹט֙ הָאִ֔ישׁ כִּֽי אִם כִּלָּ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַיּֽוֹם

translation_notes: Naomi seeks 'rest' or secure settlement for Ruth within the limited economic and marital structures available to widows. The goal is safety, not a declaration that every woman needs marriage.

The threshing floor is a nighttime workplace with food, drink, sleeping workers, and sexual ambiguity. Ruth enters a vulnerable setting; the scene must not become a universal dating, seduction, or obedience script.
'Feet' may be literal and can function euphemistically elsewhere. The Hebrew does not explicitly narrate intercourse. Translation should preserve ambiguity without sensationalizing or denying risk.
Ruth does more than obey Naomi: she identifies herself, names Boaz as redeemer, and directly asks him to spread his wing or garment over her. She articulates a kinship and economic claim.
The wing request echoes Boaz's blessing in 2:12. Divine refuge is now pressed into human responsibility: Boaz is asked to embody the protection he invoked.
Boaz's praise of Ruth as a woman of hayil—strength, worth, capability—matches the description applied to him in 2:1. It is not sexual-purity grading.

Boaz is older, wealthier, male, locally established, and able to control legal access. Ruth's courage does not erase this power imbalance or make silence and compliance equivalent to unrestricted consent.

Boaz acknowledges a nearer redeemer rather than privately taking control. The legal process protects competing family claims, though the system still treats women's futures through male-governed transactions.
His request for secrecy may protect Ruth's reputation and the legal process, but secrecy in a vulnerable nighttime encounter must never be idealized as a requirement in modern relationships.
The six measures of barley are materially significant and intentionally answer Naomi's language of emptiness. Grain is provision, not payment for sexual access.
Verse 15 has a Hebrew pronoun variation reflected in witnesses and traditions—whether he or she went into city. Later textual audit should compare the Masoretic reading and ancient versions.
safety_note: Do not use Ruth 3 to teach sexual compliance, covert encounters, age or wealth imbalance as romance, or obedience to elders over bodily autonomy. Preserve Ruth's initiative, the scene's ambiguity, Boaz's procedural restraint, and the difference between covenant responsibility and possession.
